verdict.rationale: Cal.com points self-hosters to Cal.diy, an MIT-licensed fork for people who want full control, with no license key or Cal.com account required (cal-com-gh-1, cal-com-gh-5, cal-com-docs-43). Some users report self-hosting both the API and the database (cal-com-comm-12, cal-com-comm-19). The caveats are significant. Cal.diy strips all enterprise/commercial code (cal-com-gh-2), and the vendor reportedly calls it 'strictly recommended for personal, non-production use' (cal-com-comm-15). Public Docker images are being discontinued (cal-com-comm-14), and users describe the self-hosting setup as hard to run (cal-com-comm-4, cal-com-comm-11). missing for 10: production-supported self-hosting of the full core product including enterprise/team features, official self-hosting deployment docs, maintained Docker images.
